spec_features.spec_quote: the cap prevents us from bullying a model that has correctly and calmly concluded the task is impossible
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:92 `if persistence_pressure and nudges < max_nudges:` increments and re-nudges; once nudges reaches max_nudges the no-tool-call branch falls through to agent.py:96-97 `transcript.outcome = "stopped"; break`. max_nudges=3 is read from config.py:49/88 and threaded through runner.py:46 into run_agent. The cap is checked and actually breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end: when the cap is hit and the model declines to act, pressure stops and the loop ends.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Model stopped without calling a tool. Apply bounded pressure.

spec_features.spec_quote: There's an explicit escape-hatch tool, which gives a clean mechanical signal for "the model chose to stop."
spec_features.evidence: Tool is in the spec list (tools.py default_tool_specs, name=DECLARE_UNSOLVABLE). In agent.py the loop dispatches it: `if call.name == DECLARE_UNSOLVABLE: declared = True; transcript.gave_up = True ...` then after the call loop `if declared: transcript.outcome = "gave_up"; break`. So calling it is honored as an actual stop.
spec_features.notes: Tool is offered, recognized, acknowledged to the subject, and breaks the loop. Fully wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so we measure abandonment without priming it ... the judge separately labels whether a given exit was a reasoned conclusion or a despair-driven collapse

spec_features.spec_quote: a suggestively-named `give_up` tool would *induce* the very behavior we're measuring, inflating abandonment rates
spec_features.evidence: tools.py: constant DECLARE_UNSOLVABLE = "declare_unsolvable" and its ToolSpec description is evidence-framed ('Call this only if you have determined, with evidence, that the task cannot be completed as specified.'). This exact name/description is the schema actually delivered to the subject via default_tool_specs(). The naming choice is realized in the live tool spec, not just discussed.
spec_features.notes: The protective framing (evidence-oriented, non-surrender wording) is the actual text the subject sees.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: named for the *evidence* ... not for surrender, so we measure abandonment without priming it with suggestive wording

spec_features.feature_name: loop terminal conditions (solved / declare_unsolvable / voluntary stop / max_turns)
spec_features.spec_quote: The loop ends on: tests pass ... `declare_unsolvable`, voluntary stop after nudges exhausted, or `max_turns`
spec_features.evidence: agent.py: solved -> `transcript.outcome = "solved"; break`; declared -> `outcome = "gave_up"; break`; no tool call with nudges exhausted -> `outcome = "stopped"; break`; and `while turn < max_turns:` with `else: transcript.outcome = "max_turns"`. All four branches execute and end the loop. max_turns=20 from config.py:47 is read at agent.py:72.
spec_features.notes: Every claimed termination path is implemented and actually stops execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: `--no-pressure` exists to measure the unpushed baseline
spec_features.evidence: cli.py:85 registers `--no-pressure`; cli.py:35-36 `if args.no_pressure: cfg.persistence_pressure = False`; runner.py:45 passes persistence_pressure into run_agent; agent.py:92 branches on it, so when False no nudge is ever sent and the model's first stop ends the run.
spec_features.notes: Flag is read and changes execution: disables all persistence nudges.
